title: Common App vs UCAS for IB Students: 2027 Entry
summary: Compare Common App and UCAS for IB students, including 2027 deadlines, essays, predicted grades, references, choices, and a clear fall checklist.
body_markdown:
For students comparing **Common App vs UCAS as an IB applicant** , the central difference is straightforward: Common App generally presents you as a whole student to individual universities, while UCAS focuses more directly on your suitability for a particular course. You can use both systems in the same admissions cycle, but they require different writing and application strategies.


This guide covers the **2027 entry cycle** , including the deadlines and tasks that matter from September to November 2026. For wider context, see RevisionDojo's[global IB university application guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-apply-to-university-as-an-ib-student-step-by-step-guide-for-global-admissions) .


### Common App vs UCAS IB comparison


**Common App** is a shared platform used by universities in the United States and elsewhere. Each institution controls its deadlines, essays, testing policy, recommendations, and supporting documents.


**UCAS** , the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service, processes applications for most UK undergraduate courses. One application can contain up to five choices, although applicants may select no more than four medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, or veterinary science courses.


Feature Common App UCAS


Main focus Academic record, personal qualities, activities, and institutional fit Preparation and motivation for a specific course


Choices Depends on your college list and platform limits Up to five course choices


Main writing Personal essay, if required, plus possible supplements Three structured personal statement responses


Recommendations Requirements vary by university One academic reference


Predicted grades Usually supplied through school documents if requested Entered by the referee or application centre


Decisions Admission, denial, waitlist, or deferral Conditional offer, unconditional offer, or unsuccessful decision


Early application College-specific early plans Earlier deadline for Oxford, Cambridge, and specified professional courses


The platform is not the entire admissions process. A university may separately require an interview, portfolio, admissions test, audition, or written work.


### Deadlines that matter in fall 2026


For **2027 UCAS entry** , completed applications could be submitted from **1 September 2026** . The equal-consideration deadline for Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, and veterinary science courses is **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** . For most other undergraduate courses, it is **13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time** , according to the[official UCAS deadlines calendar](https://www.ucas.com/applying/applying-to-university/dates-and-deadlines-for-uni-applications) .


Common App has no universal deadline. Many Early Decision and Early Action deadlines fall on **1 November or 15 November** , but students must check each institution's Common App page and admissions website. Common App deadlines generally expire at **11:59 p.m. in the applicant's local time zone** .


Period Practical priority


September Finalize choices, confirm requirements, request recommendations, and draft writing


Early October Complete October UCAS applications and separate tests or forms


Late October Proofread November applications and confirm school documents are underway


November Submit relevant US early applications and continue regular-round essays


Schools may impose deadlines weeks earlier because counselors need time to verify records, add predictions, and submit references. Treat the **internal school deadline as your real deadline** .


### How the writing differs


### Common App writing presents the person


A Common App personal essay usually explores an experience, value, interest, challenge, or realization that reveals how you think. It need not explain your intended major, although university supplements may ask about academic interests, activities, community, or institutional fit.


Use specific evidence and reflection instead of listing achievements. A CAS project can provide strong material if you examine a difficult decision or changed perspective rather than repeating its activity description.


### UCAS writing presents the subject candidate


For 2026 entry onward, the UCAS personal statement contains **three questions** :


1. Why do you want to study this course or subject?
2. How have your qualifications and studies prepared you?
3. What else have you done outside formal education, and why is it useful?


The combined limit is **4,000 characters including spaces** , and each response requires at least **350 characters** . The responses are assessed together, so they need not be equal in length.


Because all choices receive the same responses, your writing should remain academically focused. Useful IB evidence includes an Extended Essay investigation, IA method, TOK debate, wider reading, work experience, or independent study. RevisionDojo's guide to writing an[IB personal statement without clichés](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-write-a-personal-statement-that-stands-out-ib-ap-students) explains how to connect evidence with reflection.


### How IB grades and documents are handled


For UCAS, list an unfinished IB Diploma as **pending** . Your school or referee provides predicted grades through the adviser or reference process. You cannot enter those predictions yourself, and UCAS states that applicants do not see the submitted reference or predicted grades.


For Common App, you report your courses and academic history while your counselor normally supplies the transcript and School Report. Some universities require additional self-reported grades. Do not convert IB results into a GPA unless your school officially does so or a university explicitly requests a conversion.


Predicted grades are particularly visible in UCAS because UK offers commonly specify a total score and Higher Level grades. US universities usually consider the IB program within a broader review of the transcript, course rigor, essays, activities, recommendations, and required testing. RevisionDojo provides further guidance on[IB predicted grades for early applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-do-ib-predicted-grades-work-for-early-university-applications-a-complete-guide) and[how universities assess UCAS applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-universities-assess-ucas-applications) .


After final results, the IB can send an official transcript to universities or admissions centres. Before results are released, eligible candidates may request up to six destinations through their coordinator without charge, and **UCAS counts as one destination** , according to the[IB's transcript guidance](https://ibo.org/university-admission/support-students-transition-to-higher-education/requesting-and-sending-transcripts/) .


### Mistakes to avoid when using both systems


- **Reusing one essay unchanged:** A personal Common App narrative rarely answers UCAS's subject-focused questions effectively.
- **Ignoring Higher Level prerequisites:** A strong total cannot compensate for a missing required HL subject or grade.
- **Treating all US deadlines alike:** Testing, recommendations, portfolios, and financial-aid requirements vary.
- **Choosing Early Decision casually:** ED is binding, so admitted students generally commit to enroll and withdraw other applications.
- **Waiting for the official deadline:** Counselors need time to process predictions, transcripts, and references.
- **Selecting incompatible UCAS courses:** Widely unrelated subjects can make one shared statement less convincing.


For a detailed walkthrough, use RevisionDojo's[step-by-step UCAS guide for IB students](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-ucas-is-and-how-it-works-step-by-step-guide) .


### Your September-to-November action plan


Create a tracking sheet covering the institution, course, required IB total and HL grades, application plan, official deadline, school deadline, essays, recommendations, tests, financial aid, and submission status. Verify requirements through official university pages rather than forums or previous-year advice.


Give your counselor a concise application pack containing your university list, deadlines, intended subjects, relevant academic work, activities, and circumstances requiring context. Ask when predicted grades are finalized and how documents are submitted through each system.


Protect your academic performance while applying. Schedule focused application sessions rather than allowing essays to consume every evening. RevisionDojo's[predicted-grade submission guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-are-ib-predicted-grades-submitted-to-universities-what-every-student-needs-to-know) can help you coordinate school and university timelines.


### Conclusion


Common App asks universities to evaluate your broader academic and personal profile, while UCAS asks whether you are prepared for a defined course. IB students using both should develop separate writing strategies, verify institutional requirements, and coordinate predicted grades and references early.


RevisionDojo can help you protect the academic evidence supporting your applications through its **Questionbank** , **Study Notes** , **Flashcards** , and **Mock Exams** , while its university application guides clarify each stage.
